items.explanation: The Radicals backed military rule, Johnson's impeachment, and Black officeholding — but they sought to bar ex-Confederate leaders from power, not restore them.
options: A. Military governance of the South
B. The impeachment of Andrew Johnson
C. Restoring ex-Confederate leaders to power
D. Electing newly enfranchised Black legislators
items.stem: Radical Republicans favored all of the following EXCEPT

items.explanation: The House impeached Johnson for firing Secretary of War Stanton in defiance of the Tenure of Office Act — though the real clash was over his lenient Reconstruction policies.
options: A. Violating the Tenure of Office Act
B. Violating the Reconstruction Act
C. Pursuing too lenient a Southern policy
D. Failing to enforce the Civil Rights Act of 1866
items.stem: The stated legal ground for Andrew Johnson's impeachment was

items.explanation: Southern legislatures in 1865–66 passed Black Codes restricting Black movement, barring them from most occupations, and binding them to plantation labor — slavery in all but name.
options: A. To expand Black political participation
B. To strengthen the Freedmen's Bureau
C. To bar Black workers from many occupations
D. To preserve slavery in the Deep South

items.explanation: The 1877 bargain gave Hayes the presidency in exchange for withdrawing the last federal troops from the South, ending Reconstruction and abandoning Black Southerners to white rule.
options: A. A presidential order ended it
B. Federal troops were withdrawn from the South
C. Hayes personally opposed Reconstruction
D. Black political power made it unnecessary
items.stem: Reconstruction ended with the Compromise of 1877 because

items.explanation: Ratified in 1870, the Fifteenth Amendment barred denying the vote 'on account of race, color, or previous condition of servitude.'
options: A. Readmitted Southern states to the Union
B. Abolished slavery
C. Barred racial discrimination in voting
D. Disqualified ex-Confederate officials from office

items.explanation: Bruce, a Black senator from Mississippi, spoke during Reconstruction — the brief window when federal power protected Black political rights in the South.
options: A. The Industrial Revolution
B. The 'New' Immigration
C. Progressivism
D. Reconstruction
